item.title: Air India and AI Express cancel Riyadh, Dammam flights till Nov 7
item.description: IndiGo and Akasa Air have also cancelled their services to Saudi Arabian cities amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the region and attacks at airports in the Gulf country.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Aviation / News / Air India and AI Express cancel Riyadh, Dammam flights till Nov 7

Air India and AI Express cancel Riyadh, Dammam flights till Nov 7 IndiGo and Akasa Air have also cancelled their services to Saudi Arabian cities amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the region and attacks at airports in the Gulf country

Air India(Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 24 2026 | 11:21 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Air India and Air India Express on Saturday extended the cancellation of their flights connecting Riyadh and Dammam till November 7, while services to Jeddah will remain suspended till October 31. IndiGo and Akasa Air have also cancelled their services to Saudi Arabian cities amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the region and attacks at airports in the Gulf country. "In view of the prevailing situation in the region, Air India and Air India Express flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended until 7 November 2026, while services to and from Jeddah will remain suspended until 31 October 2026," Air India said in a post on X.   The airline said passengers holding confirmed bookings issued on or before October 24 may avail flexible rebooking options or opt for a full refund upon cancellation of their bookings. Earlier, the two airlines cancelled their services to Saudi Arabia till October 24. Also Read

IndiGo on Saturday said that after a careful assessment, flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will also remain cancelled till October 31. On Friday, the airline announced cancelling services to Riyadh till October 31, while for the other three cities, the cancellation of flights was till October 27. Akasa Air, on Friday, said it extended the suspension of flights connecting Riyadh till November 30 and to Jeddah till November 10.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank's Q2 consolidated net profit rises 26% to ₹5,645 crore
item.description: Standalone profit rose 29 per cent as NII grew 16 per cent and provisions fell, though large FCNR(B) inflows pushed net interest margin down to 4.31 per cent ...
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda
item.content:encoded: Kotak Mahindra Bank on Saturday reported a 26 per cent year-on-year (YoY) rise in consolidated net profit to ₹5,645 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), from ₹4,468 crore in Q2FY26. Sequentially, profit was up 3 per cent from ₹5,480 crore in the June quarter (Q1FY27). On a standalone basis, the bank reported a 29 per cent YoY rise in net profit to ₹4,212 crore for the September quarter (Q2FY27). The rise came on lower provisions and 16 per cent growth in net interest income (NII), even as the bank's margin contracted on inflows of foreign currency non-resident (bank) [FCNR(B)] deposits. The bank had reported a net profit of ₹3,253 crore in Q2FY26. Sequentially, profit was up 2 per cent from ₹4,123 crore in Q1FY27. Net interest income (NII) rose 16 per cent YoY to ₹8,459 crore from ₹7,311 crore in Q2FY26. Sequentially, it was up 7 per cent from ₹7,928 crore in Q1FY27. Net interest margin (NIM) stood at 4.31 per cent, against 4.54 per cent a year earlier and 4.53 per cent in Q1. The bank said the moderation was largely on account of FCNR(B) mobilisation during the quarter.  It raised FCNR(B) deposits of about ₹55,344 crore and extended loans of about ₹16,110 crore through its international branches.  Cost of funds was 4.52 per cent in Q2FY27, compared with 4.70 per cent a year ago and 4.46 per cent in Q1. Fee and services income rose 21 per cent YoY to ₹2,926 crore in Q2FY27.  Operating expenses increased 14 per cent to ₹5,271 crore.  Provisions fell 15 per cent YoY to ₹803 crore from ₹947 crore, though they were higher than ₹668 crore in Q1.  Annualised credit cost was 0.35 per cent, against 0.79 per cent in Q2FY26 and 0.46 per cent in Q1. Asset quality of the bank improved. Slippages declined 24 per cent to ₹1,230 crore in Q2FY27 from ₹1,629 crore in the year-ago period. Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) were 1.04 per cent of advances as of September 30, against 1.39 per cent a year earlier. Net NPA was 0.24 per cent, against 0.32 per cent in Q2FY26. The provision coverage ratio stood at 78 per cent, compared with 77 per cent in the year-ago quarter. Net advances grew 25 per cent to ₹5.77 trillion in Q2FY27. Excluding loans against FCNR(B) deposits and the loan portfolio acquired from Kotak Mahindra Investments (KMIL), growth was 19 per cent.  Total deposits rose 23 per cent to ₹6.51 trillion, or 13 per cent excluding FCNR(B) deposits, in the July-Sept quarter of FY27. The current account and savings account (CASA) ratio fell to 38.2 per cent in Q2FY27 from 42.3 per cent a year ago, which the bank attributed to the increase in term deposits from FCNR(B) inflows. Excluding these deposits, the ratio was 41.8 per cent. The credit-to-deposit ratio was 88.6 per cent in Q2FY27, compared with 87.5 per cent in the year-ago period. Standalone annualised return on assets (ROA) was 1.92 per cent and return on equity (ROE) was 11.65 per cent. The capital adequacy ratio was 21.9 per cent, with a CET1 ratio of 21.4 per cent. For the quarter under review, among subsidiaries, Kotak Securities reported a profit of ₹348 crore and Kotak Mahindra Prime ₹251 crore. Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance posted a profit of ₹198 crore. Kotak Asset Management and Trustee Company earned ₹287 crore in profit, while Kotak Alternate Asset Managers earned ₹87 crore in profit. (Disclosure: Entities controlled by the Kotak family have a significant holding in Business Standard Pvt Ltd)

item.description: Firms including Kotak Mahindra, AU Small Finance Bank, Kajaria Ceramics, Netweb Technologies, and Apollo Micro Systems are also to release their July-September earnings today ...
item.dc:creator: Apexa Rai
item.content:encoded: Kotak Mahindra Bank, IDFC First Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, Castrol India, JK Cement, Kajaria Ceramics, Netweb Technologies India, Apollo Micro Systems, Lumax Auto Technologies, Gujarat Ambuja Exports, and SBFC Finance are among the 33 companies scheduled to announce their financial results for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27) on Saturday.  Some other firms announcing their July to September earnings include Chembond Chemicals, Chemcon Speciality Chemicals, High Energy Batteries India, JTL Defence, Rajoo Engineers, Permanent Magnets, Seshasayee Paper and Boards, North Eastern Carrying Corporation, 3P Land Holdings, Modis Navnirman, S V Global Mill, and Damodar Industries. Infosys Q2 result highlightInfosys reported a 6.2 per cent year-on-year rise in net profit to ₹7,828 crore in Q2FY27, while revenue from operations increased 10.7 per cent to ₹49,244 crore. However, the IT services major cut its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1–2 per cent in constant currency terms from 1.5–3 per cent earlier, citing weaker growth expectations in the US and rising AI-led pricing pressures.  The company reported large deal wins worth $5.2 billion during the quarter, including a mega deal valued at more than $2 billion. AI revenue accounted for 10.5 per cent of total revenue, up from 8.2 per cent in Q1FY27, and grew 29 per cent sequentially. Operating margin remained broadly stable at around 21 per cent, while Infosys retained its FY27 operating margin guidance of 20–22 per cent.Market updates from Oct 23The Sensex and Nifty50 ended lower for the fourth consecutive session as geopolitical tensions weighed on investor sentiment.The Sensex fell 125.56 points, or 0.17 per cent, to 73,123.83, while the Nifty50 declined 87.65 points, or 0.39 per cent, to 22,600. Shriram Finance, Adani Enterprises and JSW Steel were the top losers on the Nifty50. In the broader markets, the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 2.21 per cent and 2.94 per cent, respectively. Among sectoral indices, Nifty Metal, Nifty Realty and Nifty PSU Bank underperformed, while Nifty IT was the most resilient, declining the least.Companies announcing Q2 results today3P Land Holdings LtdApollo Micro Systems LtdAU Small Finance Bank LtdCastrol India LtdChembond Chemicals LtdChemcon Speciality Chemicals LtdDachepalli Publishers LtdDamodar Industries Ltd-$Evexia Lifecare LtdGujarat Ambuja Exports LtdGerman Green Steel and Power LtdHigh Energy Batteries India LtdIDFC First Bank LtdJK Cement LtdJTL Defence LtdKajaria Ceramics LtdKotak Mahindra Bank LtdLumax Auto Technologies LtdModis Navnirman LtdNorth Eastern Carrying Corporation LtdNetweb Technologies India LtdOswal Yarns LtdPermanent Magnets Ltd-$Quanto Agroworld LtdRajoo Engineers Ltd-$SBFC Finance LtdSaptak Chem And Business LtdSeshasayee Paper and Boards LtdShangar Decor LtdSJ Corporation LtdSKP Securities LtdSovereign Diamonds LtdS V Global Mill Ltd

item.title: Swiggy Q2 net loss narrows 15.6% to ₹922 crore, revenue rises 36%
item.description: Swiggy's food delivery adjusted EBITDA rose ₹101 crore year-on-year to ₹341 crore in Q2FY27, while Instamart's gross order value grew 16.7 per cent sequentially to ₹9,230 crore.
item.dc:creator: Peerzada Abrar
item.content:encoded: Food and grocery delivery platform Swiggy on Thursday reported a 15.6 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) decline in its net loss to ₹922 crore in the second quarter (July-September/Q2) of 2026-27 (FY27), from ₹1,092 crore a year earlier. The Bengaluru-based company had posted a loss of ₹791 crore in the previous quarter. Revenue from operations rose 36 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹7,571 crore in Q2FY27, compared with ₹5,561 crore a year earlier. Revenue stood at ₹6,812 crore in the previous quarter. Swiggy’s total expenses rose nearly 30 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹8,703 crore in the quarter ended September, from ₹6,711 crore a year earlier. Expenses stood at ₹7,813 crore in the preceding quarter. “Our food delivery business delivered its highest-ever profits and margins while we continue to unlock growth in new categories through Toing, our standalone offering for affordable meals,” said Sriharsha Majety, managing director and group chief executive officer of Swiggy.  Gross order value (GOV) in the food delivery business grew 17.7 per cent Y-o-Y and 5.9 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) to ₹10,054 crore, the company said in a press release. Monthly transacting users in the food delivery segment rose 15.2 per cent Y-o-Y to 19.8 million. The segment’s adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (Ebitda) rose ₹101 crore Y-o-Y to ₹341 crore, with an adjusted Ebitda margin of 3.4 per cent of GOV, up 58 basis points (bps). Toing, Swiggy’s standalone app for affordable meals, operates in more than 50 cities. The company said two out of three new users on the platform were new to the food delivery category. Instamart’s GOV grew 16.7 per cent Q-o-Q to ₹9,230 crore. Net order value grew 13.4 per cent Q-o-Q and 31.4 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹6,594 crore. The company added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking its total to 1,240 stores covering 5.2 million square feet, up 13.3 per cent Y-o-Y. Contribution margin stood at -1 per cent of GOV, up 157 bps Y-o-Y but down 82 bps Q-o-Q. The quick-commerce (qcom) business’s adjusted Ebitda margin improved to -9.7 per cent from -9.8 per cent in the previous quarter. The business reported a loss of ₹895 crore for the quarter. The out-of-home consumption business’s GOV grew 34.9 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹1,508 crore. The business remained profitable for the seventh consecutive quarter, with a margin of 0.5 per cent of GOV. “In qcom, we delivered accelerated growth as guided and obtained the necessary approvals to qualify as an Indian-owned and controlled company,” Majety said. “We believe differentiation will decide the winners, with speed and selection becoming table stakes. We see assortment as a curation game rather than a volume game, and we aim to enable consumers to buy better, not just offer more.” In comparison, Eternal, the parent company of Zomato, reported a 92 per cent Y-o-Y rise in net profit to ₹125 crore in Q2, while its revenue from operations rose 78 per cent to ₹24,138 crore.
